The Diagnostic Radiologic Technologist, Picture Archival Communication System (PACS) operates integrated digital imaging systems across multiple modalities including General Radiology, Computerized Tomography (CT), Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI), Ultrasound, Nuclear Medicine, and Mammography.

Serves in a multi-functional role encompassing Imaging ADPAC (Automated Data Processing Application Coordinator), PACS Administrator, and Quality Assurance (QA) Technologist responsibilities.

Other duties/responsibilities include, but are not limited to the following: Serves as PACS Administrator supporting digital imaging systems including image processing, storage, retrieval, transmission, and display across all sites. Performs At least 50 percent of assigned duties in PACS Administrator functions.

Maintains system performance, functionality, and operational continuity of PACS and integrated imaging systems. Monitors system performance and capacity and adjusts operational parameters as necessary. Provides advanced troubleshooting of imaging systems, modality interfaces, display workstations, and image transmission errors.

Diagnoses system malfunctions, isolates cause and implements corrective actions or coordinates resolution with OI&T, Biomedical Engineering, and vendors. Provides support for system upgrades, implementations, and testing of new imaging technologies. Participates in contingency planning, downtime procedures, and disaster recovery operations.

Ensure system communications and interoperability across all imaging locations. Assists in the development, implementation, and oversight of Imaging Service Quality Management (QM) and QC programs. Monitors and evaluates imaging quality from acquisition through final display.

Develops data collection and analysis methods to support performance improvement and operational efficiency. Performs QC testing at required intervals (monthly, quarterly, annual) and ensures compliance with established standards. Provides objective performance data to supervisors to support staff oversight and training.

Ensures compliance with Joint Commission, Food Drug Administration (FDA), Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA), and Veterans Health Administration (VHA) standards. Provides training to Radiologists, Technologists, Clinicians, and trainees on VistA, CPRS, PACS, and imaging systems.

Coordinates training activities with CACs, system administrators, and PACS personnel. Supports affiliated academic programs and ensures appropriate system access and functionality for trainees. Serves as Imaging Service ADPAC and subject matter expert for the VistA Radiology/Nuclear Medicine package and VistA Imaging interface.

Provides long-range planning, system configuration, maintenance, and troubleshooting of VistA Radiology, DHCP packages, and Voice Recognition systems in coordination with OI&T. Builds and maintains system files including menus, security keys, HL7 interfaces, CPT codes, exam structures, workload capture, and radiology-specific configurations..

Coordinates with Clinical Application Coordinators (CACs) for CPRS integration, quick orders, and workflow optimization. Manages user access, system permissions, and system functionality across all imaging sites. Performs other duties as listed in functional statement.

Total Rewards of a Allied Health Professional The duties and responsibilities of the Diagnostic Radiologic Technologist include, but are not limited to, the following: Employee understands and complies with the laws, regulations, and industry standards which apply to their job functions and performs those functions with the highest standards of business integrity.

Performs routine radiographic procedures that may require utilization of contrast materials and sterile techniques including but not limited to general radiography, etc.

Prepares contrast materials under the direction of the radiologist for the purpose of performing exams requiring injectable solutions such as IVP, cystogram, cholangiograms, fistulagrams and arthrography and performing oral and rectal exams of the GI tract. In the case of injected media, patient consent must be obtained.

Determines technical factors, positioning, etc., to produce a high quality diagnostic image and confers with the radiologists to determine the requirements for non-standard exams that do not conform to established standard protocols. Properly identifies the patient and the image. Uses left, right and other markers when appropriate.

This is essential so that mistaken identity does not occur. The technologist must be certain that the patient ID band and the request are identical. Confirms patient identity by verbally confirming patient name and social security number. Performs radiographic exams at the bedside and/or in the operating/surgical suites.

Responsible for providing quality diagnostic images for the surgeons and/or other professional staff on patients that are unable to receive imaging services within the radiology department due to patient incapacity or surgical requirement.

Use of portable x-ray equipment, mobile intensifier units and other equipment may be required to complete the requested procedure(s).

Works with the radiologist, surgeon and/or other professional staff as a member of the radiographic team with the responsibility for anticipating technique factor difficulties, preparation of trays, preparation of contrast, supplying of required instruments and equipment (i.e. sterile packs, gloves, syringes, etc.).

Practices radiation safety (ALARA) in order to reduce exposure to the patients, employee, staff, and others. Reducing exposure time, increasing distance and utilizing shielding (i.e. lead aprons, lead gloves, lead shields, lead lined walls and collimation) will ensure compliance and minimize radiation exposure.

Responsible for wearing film badges in compliance with radiation regulations. Responsible for explaining the procedure to competent patients in a manner that is understandable to the patient and includes what is to be done as well as any potential risks or hazards.

Responsible for inventory and stocking of all general radiography supplies and other related materials. During an emergency the technologist may be requested to stay over or return to work to ensure proper and effective emergency care can be given to the patient.

Performs and/or supervises routine housekeeping duties to assure area is clean and sanitary. Must report unsanitary conditions as well as equipment malfunction in a timely manner to the supervisor.
